Name: Tan Srpka
On-map name: Srpkan Khanate (can I have it changed to just Srpka please?)
Expansion Claim: https://imgur.com/a/3jyRKtN
Size of claim: 1014 words
Population alteration: 47->58 million
GDP alteration: 962B->1.06T (16,305->18,276)
[spoiler=Expansion RP]

In 1275, the Srpkan Khanate was suffering a wave of rebellions from territories the late General Badai had conquered and occupied.  Srpka, under his command, had conquered lands across East Shamat, going from the west coast to the east coast. That was 7 years ago. Now, after his death in battle, the Srpkans had lost their great military mind, and the man never really bothered passing legislation or setting up states for the people he had steamrolled over. Now Srpka was breaking under its own weight.

It was essentially a civil war in slow motion. Over time, more and more people and ethnic groups would break away from the Khanate in what were called fractures. Finally, in 1427, the people living in the Eastern Ridge revolted against the Srpkan State, desiring to break free of the Khan and his absolutism and have a ruler from home lead their peoples.

When the people living in the Eastern Ridge, simply called ridge men by the Srpkans, began an open revolt, the Khanate could only watch. An attempt was made to try and subdue the rebellion, but it only led to a miserable defeat at the Battle of Baruun-Urt to an outnumbered rebel army. While several raids were launched against the rebel forces over two years, no significant gains or progress was made. In 1429, the Srpkans were forced to sign peace with the rebels, which formed petty but independent kingdoms in the Eastern Ridge. The Srpkan government would collapse and lose their control three months later. It seemed like the Srpkan Khanate had lost their grasp over the Eastern Ridge.

But, in 1542, the Srpkans tried again, trying to reunify after their inevitable collapse from within. The Srpkans launched three separate invasions from the north, south and center of the mountain range. These offensives were all aiming to surround Kirokez, which was the largest city of the mountain kingdoms and the main tower of command for the ridge land military forces. The northern front, assigned to Colonel Jungshoi, was the most successful, and he was chosen to lead the charge into Kirokez. The other two colonels, Khalja and Nogai, were ordered to push into territory behind the city for a full encirclement.

Kirokez was very poorly defended, being within a green spot of the mountain range and having suffered through years of warring between the petty kingdoms and their futile attempts at a united ridgeland kingdom. It also didnt help that the rebel forces had sent much of the army to try and fight the incoming Srpkan forces. The Srpkans decided to wait however, and set up hidden encampments outside the city walls. Spies were sent in over time to map out the city and its fortifications. Plans were drawn out, and after about 2 months of encampment, the Srpkans charged. 

Caught off guard, the ridgeland forces didnt have time to ask for help or reinforcements. The ridgeland forces attempted to defend the city, but the Srpkans were coming down the mountainside from three different directions. The Srpkans used their musket weaponry to wipe the defenses located on the walls, before rushing in through the gates into the city. The battle would only last for about two hours, before Srpkan forces eventually raised their flag over the city. This battle is often referred to in Srpkan poetry and song, being a quite famous and well-known battle among Srpkans, especially among those in Kirokez.

While the loss of the city wasnt technically the end for the ridgeland forces, it cut their frontlines in half, dividing between north and south. Colonel Jungshoi was put in charge of the northern front, and was promoted to Brigadier General for his deeds and actions at Kirokez. Khalja and Nogai were put in charge of the southern front and were also promoted for their actions at Kirokez. While the ridgelanders would continue to attempt to fight the Srpkans, they simply didnt have the supplies to wage war anymore.

A treaty was eventually signed with the Srpkans at Vahdat in 1543. Since there were many tiny kingdoms of the same ethnic group and people ruled by different warlords, the Khan created two different kingdoms for the two main ethnic groups of the region, the kingdoms of Qar-Shaki and Khumand respectively. The Khan promised to fund the autonomous kingdoms on the condition that they work to maintain peace and keep the warlords of the area in check, a promise he would keep his word on. This integrity from the Khan combined with the terms of the treaty would help his public image, helping to secure the throne a year later under his new house.

However, in 1792, 249 years after the integration of the eastern kingdoms into Srpka, trouble would strike again. Many Islamic peoples desired Srpka to become an Islamic style state like many of those in West Shamat. Those of other religions, especially paganism, hated this idea, and much multi religious violence was seen in Srpka, until one particularly bad event of violence sparked outrage, and eventually, a civil war.

Many different factions rose up in Srpka, among those of which included the ridgelanders who wished to separate from Srpka once again. These groups were few and far between, as the deal the ridgelanders were given was a pretty fair one. Therefore, the eastern ridge kingdom There was, however, many invasions of the far eastern kingdoms from the warring factions nearby, however.

For the most part, the eastern kingdoms were defended from the Islamic rebels, and no significant battles ever occurred on these lands, being seen as not worth attacking due to its harsher terrain and lack of valuable resources for the time. The war ended in 1800 with the signing of a new treaty that rewrote the government, attempting to prevent a civil war like the one that sparked 8 years prior ever again. 

In the Treaty of Bekongkand, the Qar-Shaki and Khumand autonomous kingdoms were formally integrated into Srpka, being reformed into provinces equal to the others in the Khanate. Srpka, after 257 years, was finally united under one banner.

[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Battle of Aduab - day 7-11[/b]]
Only around 550 Sal-Baliz soldiers remained to defend the citadel, but the great building was rigged with traps, and many entrances were blocked with walls of bricks, funneling Hydronian soldiers into killzones. The dungeons of the citadel, intentionally flooded by the Sal-Baliz terrorists, became the arena for the most intense and bloody close quarter encounters in the fight for the citadel. The top levels and the towers of the citadel had their stairways blocked by machine gun nests. Hydronian infantry struggled greatly to clear out the nests, even when attempting to attack from the roof of the citadel, and Hydronian command decided to just bomb the enemy inside into submission on Day 8. Once the dungeons were cleared, the Hydronians evacuated to a safe distance, and artillery started their barrages, collapsing many of the towers and the top levels of the citadel. The Sal-Baliz who were not crushed under the rocks rushed out and were immediately gunned down by Hydronian forces - Whether the Sal-Baliz tried to surrender or launch a suicidal charge is unknown, they were not given time to do either. Some soldiers reported that the Sal-Baliz walked out unarmed and with their arms raised, others claim that they ran out with loaded weapons, shouting war cries. Hydronian command has neither denied nor confirmed either claim, and has instead chosen to ignore the issue altogether.

The fall of the citadel sparked something within the ranks of the Sal-Baliz - For the first time in the battle, THEP soldiers were under the receiving end of an artillery barrage from obsolete 20th century pieces and makeshift rocket launchers, both were almost immediately disabled by THEP close air support. The intent was to clear out possible THEP positions around the entrances of the city's complex tunnel system, allowing militia and soldiers to pour out. Hydronian and Bobian forces had to both defend the island from the counter-attack, and cover the retreat of the bridge layers, isolating THEP forces in the island, though that served as an advantage. The attempted crossing of the river by Sal-Baliz forces outside of the island turned them into easy targets for helicopters and machine guns positioned on the walls.

The biggest challenge for the THEP came on Day 9, when the Sal-Baliz detonated explosives in the great mosque in an attempt to deny it to the enemy, burying the Bobian soldiers inside as well. A complicated operation followed, with Bobian forces having to both defend the mosque and the walls from the Sal-Baliz counter-attack while at the same time trying to free the infantry stuck under the rubble of the great mosque. The THEP air force worked overtime, doing all it could to help the ground forces hold against the onslaught. The operation continued to Day 11, with constant fighting day and night - Out of the 43 soldiers fighting inside the religious building, only 12 managed to escape, the rest either crushed by the rubble, or suffocated before help could arrive. By sunset, the Sal-Baliz attack had waned, and practically ceased, those in the militia who were not executed for treason or cowardice either deserted or surrendered to the THEP army, and the main army evacuated the city in full. Some remnants of resistance still fought, especially in the eastern parts of the city. Small patrols were sent to clear out the spots one by one, until finally, Aduab was under full THEP control.

Later intelligence proved that the supreme leader had fled the city to the industrial town of Al-Sharwa, which would be the next target for THEP attacks.
[/spoiler]

[b][i]UFO SIGHTINGS INCREASED DURRING WAR TIME[/i][/b]

As The war over the fate of [nation]Sikirsk[/nation] rages on, there have been some strange reports coming in from their capital, and this entrepid reporter went all the way out to investigate.
UFO sightings have been a thing for as long as there  have been people to look up and not be sure of what it is they're looking at. From flying saucers to the strange historical phenomenon of people spotting blue police boxes through out history, you'll be hard pressed to find anyone who takes these claims seriously.
However, the timing of these sightings has many considering more mundane, albeit more gruesome theories. Bomber planes, or electronic warfare platforms have been kicked around.
I had gone down in hopes of catching sight of one myself, but I wasn't able to. Though I did feel the hostility rising from the people of Nestor Sikirsk. This war has left many people agitated, scared, and hopeless for the future. Perhaps a silly story about space aliens will help, though my editor still questions the news worthiness of this story...

(OOC: Enkia is flying sorties with their Spy Planes over Sikirskian targets, due to the inexperience of the pilots, some have been spotted by the public and misidentified as alien spacecraft.)
